Answer: C
Reason: The arrowheads in Figure 1b highlight a smooth, well-defined widening of the lower posterior mediastinum with lateral displacement of the paraspinal lines, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a neurogenic tumor (e.g., schwannoma) in this location. The absence of respiratory symptoms and the smooth margins make malignancy or abscess less likely, while the unilateral nature argues against extramedullary hematopoiesis.
